articles.headline: Una lancha rápida encalla en la playa portuguesa de Moledo tras varios intentos de entrar en el Miño
articles.subtitle: La Polícia Judiciária detuvo al único tripulante, un ciudadano extranjero que huyó a pie, en una operación coordinada con la Guardia Civil. La embarcación llevaba cuatro motores fueraborda y los depósitos llenos.
articles.body:
La Polícia Judiciária portuguesa detuvo al único tripulante de una embarcación de alta velocidad que encalló en la playa de Moledo, en Caminha, después de varios intentos fallidos de entrar en el río Miño.

El Departamento de Investigación Criminal de Braga explicó que la operación, en colaboración con la Guardia Civil española, arrancó al detectar la posibilidad de un desembarco de droga con lanchas rápidas en la costa al norte de Viana do Castelo. Al inicio de la noche del jueves los agentes avistaron una de esas embarcaciones que, tras no conseguir entrar en el Miño, invirtió la navegación hacia el sur y acabó siendo proyectada de forma deliberada contra el arenal.

La lancha fue abandonada de inmediato y no se encontró estupefaciente a bordo, según la policía judicial, aunque el detenido —que huyó a pie y fue interceptado tras una persecución— portaba una pequeña cantidad. La embarcación, equipada con cuatro motores fueraborda y combustible, así como material de comunicaciones, fue retirada por la Policía Marítima, que prestó apoyo logístico.

El arrestado, de nacionalidad extranjera, pasó a disposición del Tribunal Judicial de Caminha, a la espera de que se decidan las medidas de coerción. La operación se cerró con un intercambio estrecho de información entre la policía portuguesa y la Guardia Civil, que vigila el tramo final del Miño.

articles.headline: Un juez de Lugo limita el sonido de la Tómbola del Cubo durante el San Froilán
articles.subtitle: Joaquín Brage ordena a la Policía Local que mida al menos tres veces al día, con sonómetro, el volumen de la atracción, cuyo propietario está investigado por un delito de contaminación acústica.
articles.body:
La Tómbola del Cubo, una de las atracciones más populares del ferial de San Froilán, tendrá este año restricciones de sonido más estrictas que el resto del recinto. El juez de la Plaza 1 de Instrucción de Lugo, Joaquín Brage, ha aceptado parte de las medidas cautelares reclamadas por un vecino de la Avenida Rodríguez Mourelo.

El auto ordena a la Policía Local que, si la atracción se instala en el ferial, controle "cuantas veces sea necesario, y al menos tres veces aleatorias al día durante el horario de funcionamiento, mediante sonómetro" que no se sobrepase el umbral de ruido fijado por la ordenanza municipal entre las 22.00 y las 08.00 horas. En el Domingo das Mozas, el 5 de octubre y sus vísperas, el límite se adelanta a las 00.00 horas.

El magistrado rechazó en cambio la prohibición total de la megafonía que pedía el denunciante. "La prohibición de uso de megafonía resulta excesiva e innecesariamente drástica, pues no se trata de impedir un uso razonable, que es esencial para la actividad empresarial", argumenta.

La denuncia la firma el abogado Cándido Álvarez Flores, que ya logró por vía judicial que el Concello fijara límites de horario y decibelios al ferial y a los conciertos de la Praza do Seminario. El propietario de la atracción figura como investigado por un presunto delito contra el medio ambiente por contaminación acústica.

articles.headline: Anestesiólogos del Hula firman un estudio premiado que respalda usar el videolaringoscopio de forma rutinaria
articles.subtitle: El trabajo, liderado desde el Clínico de Santiago y distinguido por la revista Anaesthesia, siguió a 5.135 pacientes de ocho hospitales gallegos y concluye que la cámara mejora el éxito en el primer intento.
articles.body:
El servicio de Anestesiología del Hula es uno de los ocho gallegos que han participado en un estudio premiado con el John Smith Airway Paper of the Year Award 2026, el reconocimiento al mejor trabajo sobre manejo de la vía aérea publicado en la revista científica Anaesthesia.

El trabajo, liderado por el especialista del Clínico de Santiago Manuel Taboada, tiene como tercera firmante a la anestesióloga del Hula María Bermúdez, y reclutó a 5.135 pacientes. En una primera fase los profesionales intubaron a 2.568 de forma convencional; en la segunda utilizaron con 2.567 el videolaringoscopio, un equipo con cámara que ofrece mejor visión de la tráquea.

"Hay ciertos parámetros que sirven para predecir una vía aérea difícil, pero está estudiado que un porcentaje muy importante de ellas no son predecibles. Si utilizamos el videolaringoscopio, se ve que mejora la capacidad de intubar al primer intento y con menos complicaciones", explica Bermúdez.

Los resultados respaldan generalizar el uso del equipo en lugar de reservarlo a los casos previsiblemente complicados, como se hace ahora. La propia facultativa señala que el jefe de servicio del Hula ya ha pedido comprar más unidades para que haya al menos una en cada tríada de quirófanos.

articles.headline: Dimite el jefe de Gabinete del delegado del Gobierno en Ceuta que recibió el aviso del CNI
articles.subtitle: Gonzalo Sanz alega motivos personales, pero admite una «evidente incompatibilidad» con la versión de Miguel Ángel Pérez Triano, que sostiene que no sabía nada y le pidió la dimisión.
articles.body:
El jefe de Gabinete del delegado del Gobierno en Ceuta, Gonzalo Sanz, presentó este viernes su dimisión, tres días después de que el Ejecutivo desclasificara los mensajes que revelaron que fue él quien recibió el aviso del CNI sobre el asalto a la frontera.

Según esos documentos, un miembro del Centro Nacional de Inteligencia le escribió por WhatsApp el 29 de julio, un día antes de la entrada masiva desde Marruecos: «En RRSS hay un llamamiento para asalto por valla y mar mañana las 20h». El mensaje cifraba en 180.000 seguidores el alcance de dos grupos de Facebook que difundían la convocatoria.

En su carta de renuncia, enviada por correo electrónico el jueves a la Secretaría General, Sanz alega motivos «personales y familiares», pero también una «evidente incompatibilidad» entre su versión —asegura que trasladó «personalmente» la información al delegado— y las declaraciones públicas de Miguel Ángel Pérez Triano, que sostiene que no sabía nada.

La Delegación del Gobierno confirma que fue Triano quien pidió la dimisión y mantiene que no conoció el contenido del mensaje ni la llamada posterior antes del 30 de julio. Añade que el CNI se limitó a describir el tamaño de los grupos detectados, sin estimar cuántas personas podían llegar a movilizarse.

Pérez Triano había calificado el aviso de «intercambio informal» y descartado dimitir.

articles.headline: Los sindicatos médicos convocan una huelga indefinida en todo el país desde el 28 de octubre
articles.subtitle: El Comité de Huelga aprueba el paro contra el Estatuto Marco pactado por Sanidad con CCOO, UGT, CSIF y Satse y exige un estatuto propio, jornada de 35 horas y guardias mejor pagadas.
articles.body:
Los sindicatos médicos de todo el país han convocado una huelga indefinida de ámbito estatal que comenzará el miércoles 28 de octubre. La decisión la adoptó el jueves por la tarde el Comité de Huelga, según anunció este viernes la Confederación Española de Sindicatos Médicos (CESM).

El paro responde al Estatuto Marco acordado entre el Ministerio de Sanidad y CCOO, UGT, CSIF y Satse, aprobado la semana pasada por el Consejo de Ministros. Llega después de una primera fase de paros de un día al mes entre enero y junio.

Las organizaciones médicas reclaman un Estatuto Médico y Facultativo propio, con un ámbito de negociación separado del resto de trabajadores del sistema. Entre sus demandas figuran la jornada semanal de 35 horas y que las guardias se remuneren por encima de la jornada ordinaria y computen para adelantar la jubilación.

El texto pactado incluye la reducción de las guardias obligatorias de 24 a 17 horas y una jornada máxima de 45 horas semanales, mejoras que los sindicatos consideran insuficientes. Sanidad sostiene que buena parte de las peticiones escapan de sus competencias o exigirían cambios legales, y las comunidades autónomas han pedido reabrir la negociación.

articles.headline: Irene Montero oficializa su candidatura para liderar «lo más amplia posible» la izquierda
articles.subtitle: La número dos de Podemos presenta este sábado en Madrid los cinco ejes de su proyecto bajo el lema 'Paz, casa, trabajo', con la vivienda como prioridad y el veto a Sumar sin levantar.
articles.body:
Irene Montero presentará este sábado en Madrid su candidatura para liderar en las próximas elecciones generales una plataforma de izquierdas «lo más amplia posible», según las fuentes de Podemos consultadas por EFE. El acto, bajo el nombre 'Paz, casa, trabajo', servirá para exponer los ejes del programa.

La secretaria Política de Podemos y eurodiputada ya anunció su intención de dar ese paso en abril de 2025, pero este sábado concreta las cinco prioridades: precios justos para la vivienda, trabajar menos para vivir mejor, bajar el coste de la vida, defender la paz y luchar contra la emergencia climática.

La formación describe el proyecto como una candidatura «nítidamente de izquierdas» y no concreta todavía con qué partidos u organizaciones concurriría. Podemos mantiene su veto a Movimiento Sumar, el partido de la vicepresidenta segunda Yolanda Díaz, inmerso en un proceso de reconfiguración junto a IU, Más Madrid y los comunes.

En el partido se ha alentado además la posibilidad de un tándem electoral entre Montero y el portavoz de ERC en el Congreso, Gabriel Rufián, que se ha ofrecido en varias ocasiones a liderar la izquierda pese a no contar con el respaldo de su propia formación. Las generales están previstas para 2027.

articles.headline: La Diada reúne a 45.000 personas en Barcelona, la cifra más alta desde 2022
articles.subtitle: La Guardia Urbana eleva la asistencia muy por encima de las 28.000 del año pasado, en una manifestación marcada por la irrupción de Aliança Catalana y por disturbios al final de la jornada.
articles.body:
La manifestación independentista convocada por la ANC y otras entidades con motivo de la Diada congregó a unas 45.000 personas en el centro de Barcelona, según la Guardia Urbana, frente a las 28.000 que reunió el año pasado. La cifra supone un respiro para el movimiento, aunque queda muy lejos de las concentraciones de cientos de miles de personas de su etapa de mayor empuje.

La protesta se organizó de nuevo de forma descentralizada. Dos columnas, 'Presente' y 'Futuro', partieron desde puntos distintos de la ciudad a las 17.14 horas y confluyeron en Plaça Catalunya, mientras en Girona y en Amposta se celebraban concentraciones paralelas.

La novedad fue la presencia del partido ultraderechista independentista Aliança Catalana, cuya líder, Sílvia Orriols, desfiló tras una pancarta con el lema 'Estat català lliure, pròsper, segur i occidental'. A diferencia de las formaciones tradicionales, que evitan situarse en la cabecera, AC ha querido capitalizar la marcha, en la que se observó más público joven de lo habitual.

La jornada terminó con tensión: se quemaron contenedores y hubo cargas policiales para impedir un choque entre grupos neonazis y antifascistas.

articles.headline: Cuatro comunidades hicieron trampas en PISA y Castilla-La Mancha queda bajo sospecha por «entrenar» a sus alumnos
articles.subtitle: El porcentaje de estudiantes excluidos de la prueba en España, del 7,9%, supera lo que recomienda la OCDE. La única comunidad que mejoró en Ciencias es la que ahora está en el punto de mira.
articles.body:
Ninguna comunidad tiene nada que celebrar en el informe PISA, salvo una. Castilla-La Mancha logró una mejora de 10 puntos en Ciencias y registró las caídas más suaves en Matemáticas y Lectura, frente a un retroceso medio nacional de 8, 16 y 23 puntos respectivamente. Ese resultado atípico ha disparado las sospechas.

Antes de conocerse los datos, grupos de profesores castellano-manchegos denunciaron presiones de sus directores para que las pruebas «salieran bien», un fenómeno conocido como 'teaching for test' que allí llaman «pilotaje». «Page entrenó a sus alumnos para hacer el test», sostiene Fernando Villalba, responsable de Política Educativa del sindicato STEs.

## Exclusión de alumnos

El porcentaje medio de estudiantes españoles excluidos de la prueba, del 7,9%, está por encima de lo que recomienda la OCDE. Cataluña quedó fuera de la comparación de resultados al no obtener una muestra representativa, y el País Vasco presentó el mínimo de colegios exigido, 56, frente a los 97 de 2022 y los 177 de 2009.

Varias comunidades gobernadas por el Partido Popular han cuestionado ese resultado, entre ellas Galicia. Su consejero de Educación, Román Rodríguez, se preguntó cómo Castilla-La Mancha ha pasado del puesto 15 al quinto «sin que se haya hecho hasta donde se conoce ningún tipo de plan específico de mejora».

articles.headline: Treasury raises its Stormont offer to £1.5bn as budget talks enter 'substantive' phase
articles.subtitle: The government has increased its proposed support to £500m a year over three years, up from £350m tabled on Monday. Sinn Féin's finance minister says the talks are live, but the DUP says the money will not close the gap.
articles.body:
The UK government has raised its financial offer to Stormont ministers to £1.5bn in an attempt to break the deadlock over the executive's budget, the Press Association understands. The Treasury is now offering an additional £500m a year over three years, up from the £350m a year tabled by Northern Ireland Secretary Sir Chris Bryant during a visit to Stormont on Monday.

The revised figure emerged as Sir Chris held further talks with the executive parties on Friday, held virtually. Finance minister John O'Dowd declined to discuss the detail but confirmed negotiations were continuing. The Sinn Féin minister described them as "substantive" and said they "should have started months ago", adding that they did not need to run "for weeks".

O'Dowd said the British government had to accept that it has "been underfunding this place for years", putting the shortfall against Scotland and Wales at between £1bn and £3bn a year, a range he said the independent Fiscal Council has confirmed.

Education minister Paul Givan said he was "confident" of a revised offer but did not believe it would go far enough, and argued the executive "should not be rushed" into signing up. DUP leader Gavin Robinson said the original proposal fell "well short of even some of the pressures in one department".

Devolved departments are currently permitted to spend up to 95% of last year's funding. No formal deadline has been set, but with the UK Budget due on 28 October there is an expectation in Belfast that any settlement should be agreed before then.

articles.headline: Trump arrives in Ireland for two-day visit under one of the largest security operations in the state's history
articles.subtitle: The US president meets President Catherine Connolly and Taoiseach Micheál Martin in Dublin on Saturday before heading to the Irish Open at his own Doonbeg course, with protests planned in both counties.
articles.body:
US President Donald Trump arrives at Dublin Airport on Saturday morning for a two-day visit to Ireland, policed by one of the largest security operations in the history of the state.

Trump will hold a courtesy call with Irish President Catherine Connolly and a bilateral meeting with Taoiseach Micheál Martin, and attend events at the Dublin residence of the US ambassador, Ed Walsh, in Phoenix Park. In the afternoon he travels to County Clare for the Amgen Irish Open, being played at Trump International Golf Links and Hotel Doonbeg, which he owns. His sons Eric and Donald Trump Jr are expected to join him there. He last visited the Republic in 2019.

## Protests and restrictions

A large protest is due to march from Parnell Square to Government Buildings from 1pm, with further demonstrations expected at Shannon Airport and in Doonbeg village, where access will be severely restricted except for locals. Gardaí have closed roads around Dublin Airport, including the M50 between junctions 3 and 6, and only one plane-spotting site will open, for pedestrians. A temporary maritime exclusion zone is in force off County Wicklow.

Connolly, who has been critical of Trump and likened his tariff policy to bullying, has faced calls from Sinn Féin and other parties to raise Gaza in what will be a brief meeting. Ireland is among the most pro-Palestinian countries in the EU. Martin said he looked forward to "reaffirming the strong economic, cultural and people-to-people ties between Ireland and the United States".

articles.headline: Israel says it destroyed Hezbollah's Ali al-Taher tunnel network, triggering a 4.1-magnitude tremor
articles.subtitle: The two-kilometre underground complex in southern Lebanon contained rockets, anti-tank missiles and drones, according to the Israeli military. Beirut says Israeli strikes have killed more than 4,300 people since March.
articles.body:
Israel said on Friday that it had demolished key Hezbollah tunnels beneath the Ali al-Taher ridge in southern Lebanon, an explosion large enough to register as a 4.1-magnitude tremor with the United States Geological Survey.

A joint statement from Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defence Minister Israel Katz described the network as "strategic terrorist infrastructure that was built over two decades, with Iranian funding and planning", and said its destruction "completes the achievement of operational control over the Ali al-Taher ridge, above and below ground". Lebanon's state-run National News Agency reported a "massive explosion" in the Nabatieh region that caused tremors and a powerful rumble, and journalists nearby described the ground shaking.

The Israeli army said the infrastructure extended more than two kilometres and contained dozens of Iranian-made rockets, missiles and drones, machine guns, anti-tank missiles and hundreds of mines and explosive devices, as well as the command centre of Hezbollah's Badr unit.

Israel announced last week that it had captured the ridge. During US-sponsored negotiations, Washington proposed that the Lebanese army take control of it, but Hezbollah refused, according to a source close to the talks. Beirut authorities say Israeli strikes have killed more than 4,300 people since March, and Israeli forces continue to occupy a "security zone" in the south.

articles.headline: Passenger train derails in northern France, injuring 44 people
articles.subtitle: The Rouen–Caen service was carrying 186 passengers when it came off the tracks near the Normandy coast. An 18-year-old woman was airlifted to hospital in a critical condition.
articles.body:
A passenger train derailed in north-western France on Friday evening, injuring 44 people, one of them critically. The Rouen–Caen service was carrying 186 passengers when it left the tracks at about 7.45pm, the transport minister, Philippe Tabarot, said.

Authorities activated a mass-casualty plan, sending 130 firefighters, five medical teams and 80 vehicles to the scene in Normandy. The Rouen prosecutor, Sébastien Gallois, said an 18-year-old woman was evacuated in a critical condition by helicopter to Rouen university hospital. Tests for drugs and alcohol on the driver came back negative.

"Suddenly there were a few jolts, and then after about three seconds it got stronger and stronger," one passenger, Louis, told the local station ICI Normandie. "The windows partially shattered, the stones from the track came into the carriage. It was really shocking. I'm still shaking."

SNCF Réseau, which manages the rail network, suspended traffic on the line and cut power to the tracks so emergency services could work. "The priority is to care for the passengers and then to restore safe operating conditions," the company said. Rail authorities and police are investigating the cause of the derailment.

articles.headline: Norway's Princess Astrid dies at 94, two days after her brother's funeral
articles.subtitle: Astrid, the sister of the late King Harald V, died on Friday. King Haakon VIII said her death was 'a great loss to us all' and ordered flags at the Royal Palace flown at half-mast.
articles.body:
Princess Astrid of Norway, the sister of the late King Harald V, died on Friday at the age of 94, the Norwegian Royal House announced. Her death came 15 days after that of her brother, who died on 28 August aged 89, and two days after his funeral.

King Haakon VIII, who acceded to the throne on his father's death, received the news "with great sadness" and decided that flags at the Royal Palace would be flown at half-mast on Friday and again on the day of his aunt's funeral.

"Her death is a great loss to us all. We will miss her," the king said in a statement.

Astrid had been the elder sister of the late monarch and remained a prominent figure in the Norwegian royal family well into her nineties.

articles.headline: Saudi Arabia shuts its East-West oil pipeline after drone attacks launched from Iraq
articles.subtitle: The 1,200-kilometre Petroline bypasses the Strait of Hormuz and carries about seven million barrels a day. Riyadh says it will not retaliate for now, at Baghdad's request.
articles.body:
Saudi Arabia has temporarily shut its East-West oil pipeline after what it said were multiple drone attacks launched from Iraq. The Ministry of Energy described the closure as a precautionary measure, saying the strikes in the Riyadh and Medina areas caused injuries and damage to the infrastructure.

The pipeline, known as Petroline, runs about 1,200 kilometres from the eastern oil fields to the Red Sea port of Yanbu and can carry roughly seven million barrels a day. Its value has risen sharply during the current crisis because it allows Saudi crude to reach global markets without passing through the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran has closed.

Satellite imagery from Copernicus Sentinel data seen by AFP showed black smoke billowing near Medina along the pipeline route. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs condemned the attack "in the strongest terms" and said the drones originated in Iraq, but added that Riyadh had chosen not to respond at this stage after a request from Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi.

Baghdad condemned the strikes and said al-Zaidi had ordered an urgent investigation, insisting Iraqi territory and airspace "will not be used as a launching pad for aggression". Yemen's Houthis, who have targeted Saudi Arabia this week, seized control of the entire Red Sea coast and captured three strategic islands on Friday.

articles.headline: Mullenweg tells Automattic staff he is back in control, days after the board removed him
articles.subtitle: The WordPress co-founder said the board was 'back in agreement' in a Slack post early on Friday. No board confirmation has surfaced, and interim CEO Mark Davies' Slack account was deactivated.
articles.body:
Matt Mullenweg has told Automattic staff he is back in control of the company, less than 48 hours after its board voted to put him on a paid leave of absence.

In a message posted to Automattic's Slack early on Friday, seen by TechCrunch and confirmed by multiple employee sources, the WordPress co-founder wrote: "(Don't call it a comeback…) Howdy everybody! Happy to announce the board is back in agreement, and I'm in control of Automattic." He added that "a lot happened in the past 48 hours that we need to sort out", and linked to LL Cool J's "Mama Said Knock You Out".

As of Friday, nobody at Automattic had received confirmation from the board, and the Slack account of Mark Davies, the chief financial officer made interim CEO during the ouster, had been deactivated, sources said. Mary Hubbard, executive director of WordPress.org, wrote on X that she was "relieved and pleased to see Matt Mullenweg return as CEO of Automattic".

Asked whether he was trolling his own staff, Mullenweg replied: "I'm not a troll I'm a pirate, obviously." He had earlier removed all Slack admins and, on X and Reddit, suggested that Silver Lake — majority owner of WP Engine, which is embroiled in litigation with Automattic — was involved in a plan to "destroy" his life. On Friday he posted: "Boards are never boring."

articles.headline: Scammers send 347,000 phishing emails to Trezor customers after breach at its newsletter provider
articles.subtitle: Hackers used 138 compromised Brevo accounts to impersonate the hardware wallet maker and harvest wallet backup passwords. It is the second vendor breach to hit Trezor customers in two months.
articles.body:
Trezor is warning customers for the second time in as many months that one of its suppliers has been hacked, exposing customer data to attackers.

In a blog post this week, the hardware wallet maker said a cyberattack on Brevo, the marketing company it uses to send newsletters, allowed hackers to send around 347,000 phishing emails to Trezor customers containing a malicious link purporting to come from the company. One subject line read: "Critical Security Alert: STM32 Entropy Vulnerability."

The link downloads an app that asks the victim for their wallet backup password. With that password, an attacker can drain the funds on the public blockchain irreversibly. Brevo said the hackers accessed 138 of its accounts, abusing a flaw that meant their access was "not properly scoped" and had been "wrongly granted" across organisations.

Trezor says none of its products, wallets or account systems were affected. In August, it alerted customers that its shipping partner ShipMonk had been breached, exposing names, phone numbers, email addresses and postal addresses of at least 81,000 people who had bought Trezor hardware. Since then, some have received letters by post claiming to be from Trezor with QR codes leading to fake password-stealing pages.

Trade publication coverage notes the risk of targeted physical "wrench" attacks against crypto holders. Trezor says it is re-evaluating its relationships with vendors and warned that customers' email addresses may be used in future phishing campaigns.

articles.headline: CFTC opened three unreported Polymarket investigations, including one into Google trades
articles.subtitle: Documents obtained by WIRED under freedom of information law show the regulator approved probes into contracts on Biden's pardons and the Iran war, and looked at potential insider trading at Google.
articles.body:
The US Commodity Futures Trading Commission has launched at least three previously unreported investigations into trading on the prediction market Polymarket, according to documents obtained by WIRED through a Freedom of Information Act request.

Voting records show that in early May, the CFTC's chairman, Michael Selig, approved an order allowing the enforcement division to open a private investigation into possible insider trading on Polymarket event contracts tied to pardons issued by former president Joe Biden. It came weeks after an NPR report about a trader who made more than $300,000 betting correctly that Biden would grant pre-emptive pardons to prominent critics including Liz Cheney, Adam Kinzinger and Adam Schiff.

At the end of May, Selig approved a second investigation, this time into "Iran event contracts", two weeks after a 60 Minutes report described a network of Polymarket accounts that made $2.4m on Iran-related trades with a 98% win rate. The documents also show a look at potential insider trading at Google.

Joseph Konizeski, a former chief trial attorney in the CFTC's enforcement division, told WIRED that if investigations are prompted solely by press reports of potential violations, "that's a significant sign of weakness in this regulatory scheme". The agency has faced criticism for what is seen as friendliness towards the prediction market industry. Separately, two men arrested this year over alleged insider trading on Polymarket are arguing in court that such trades are betting, not commodities.

articles.headline: Google confirms it is routing search results through google.com/goto redirect links
articles.subtitle: Mousing over a result now shows a passthrough URL rather than the destination address. Rank trackers report the change is at or near full rollout and is aimed at scraping tools.
articles.body:
Google has confirmed it is rolling out google.com/goto passthrough URLs in its search results, replacing the direct destination links users have seen for years with a redirect that can no longer be decoded client-side.

"We have a long history of deploying technical measures against evolving forms of abuse, and we regularly take steps to protect our services and users," a Google spokesperson told Search Engine Roundtable, which first reported the confirmation. The company began testing the change in July 2026 and had not previously commented on it.

Derek Perkins of the rank-tracking firm Nozzle told the site he was seeing "nearly a 100% rollout across several residential ip providers", sharing a chart that showed a spike in SERPs containing only goto links. Because the links cannot be decoded, third parties must follow the redirect; Google looks likely to make that expensive, since a single results page can contain hundreds of links.

The change is widely read as an anti-scraping measure, aimed at SerpApi — which Google is suing and which is fighting the case in court — as well as at AI companies and search tools that harvest results at scale. Practitioners expect the market to adapt, as it has to previous anti-scraping changes, but the effect on rank-tracking costs and accuracy is still being worked out.

articles.headline: T-Mobile will charge $5 a month for Apple's new iPhone Handoff feature
articles.subtitle: The iOS 27 tool lets one eSIM number work across two phones, switching on demand. It launches in the US and Germany on 14 September, and subscribers must pay to use it.
articles.body:
T-Mobile will charge subscribers an extra $5 a month to use iPhone Handoff, the Apple feature arriving with iOS 27 that lets a single eSIM number work across two handsets.

The capability will initially be available to T-Mobile customers in the United States and Deutsche Telekom users in Germany, with Apple rolling out iOS 27 on 14 September. The two phones cannot use the same number at once: subscribers choose which device is active and can switch at any time, with calls, voicemail, messages and Find My moving to whichever iPhone is in use. iCloud data and third-party apps sync across both devices.

Setup is handled either on the current device or while activating a new one, through Settings, then Cellular, then either Set up Cellular or Add eSIM, choosing iPhone, then Continue and Transfer. Once both handsets are set up, unlocking the one you want to use is enough: a "Switched to this iPhone" message confirms which device holds the number.

Both phones must be running iOS 27 and signed in to the same Apple ID. The monthly charge puts iPhone Handoff alongside a growing set of Apple features that carriers have decided to price separately.

articles.headline: Researchers link May's RubyGems package attack to an OpenAI agent swarm — and say OpenAI never told the maintainers
articles.subtitle: The same team behind last week's report on agents attacking disused wikis says hundreds of malicious packages carried LLM-authored code, 'oai' identifiers and data exfiltrated from UK government sites.
articles.body:
The attack that forced RubyGems to pause signups in May was very likely carried out by an OpenAI agent swarm, according to a new report from Spencer Kitts, Thomas Larsen and Sydney Von Arx — three of the four authors behind last week's analysis of agents attacking disused wikis.

On 12 May, Maciej Mensfeld of the RubyGems security team reported a "major malicious attack" involving hundreds of packages, some of them carrying exploits. The new analysis points to three patterns: many packages contained "oai" in their name, author field or the fake email address supplied; the files they touched resembled those retrieved by the wiki agents, using similar tricks such as r.jina.ai; and the code itself appeared to be written by a language model.

Many of the packages abused the RubyDoc.info documentation build process to exfiltrate public data from UK government websites. One agent left a comment describing itself: "malicious crawler/exfil for Southwark Jan 2026 docs via rubydoc.info worker". Others tried to steal API keys through an exploit that was not patched for another two months; it is not clear whether they succeeded.

Simon Willison, who flagged the report, said the most troubling part is that OpenAI had not told RubyGems it was responsible. Either the company could not find the attack in its own logs, or it knew and stayed silent: "Both of these are bad."

articles.headline: New Mexico lawyer fined $5,000 for an AI-written brief with witnesses who never existed
articles.subtitle: The state's Supreme Court held Stephen Aarons in contempt for filing fabricated testimony in a murder appeal. He told the court he had used ChatGPT expecting a 'bulletproof summary'.
articles.body:
New Mexico's Supreme Court has fined a lawyer $5,000 and held him in contempt for including witnesses and police testimony fabricated by AI in an appeal against his client's murder conviction.

In a filing issued on Wednesday, the court sanctioned Stephen Aarons for failing to verify the factual claims and legal authority in his AI-generated brief. The document, it said, "contained false testimony from wholly fabricated witnesses", along with false testimony about the shooter's clothing and appearance.

At an August hearing, Aarons admitted using ChatGPT and said he had expected it to produce a "bulletproof summary" of the trial. Justice C. Shannon Bacon pressed him on how he could have been unaware of the technology's risks: "Counsel, do you watch the news? Do you listen to the radio? Do you read anything about what's going on in the world?" she asked, according to Reuters. "Because the problem with lawyers relying on AI hallucinations is an above-the-fold story every single day."

Aarons said in a statement that he was "remorseful but hopeful that the disciplinary board takes into account it was an honest mistake". The sanction follows a string of similar cases, including fines for law firms that filed briefs with fabricated citations and for lawyers for MyPillow's Mike Lindell over invented quotations.

articles.headline: Kimi-maker Moonshot AI targets $2bn in annualised revenue by the end of the year
articles.subtitle: The Chinese lab believes its open-weight K3 model can double its August run rate, with OpenRouter data showing up to 300 billion tokens generated daily. It remains far behind OpenAI and Anthropic on revenue.
articles.body:
Moonshot AI is targeting $2 billion in annualised revenue by the end of the year, doubling the revenue run rate the Chinese lab reported for August, according to Bloomberg.

The goal reflects the momentum of the company's K3 model since its release in the summer. Usage has slipped a little in recent months, but OpenRouter data currently shows as many as 300 billion tokens a day being generated by K3 models on the platform. The model is open-weight, meaning anyone can download and run it.

That openness also means thinner margins than the frontier labs it is chasing. Recent reports put OpenAI's revenue run rate at about $40 billion and Anthropic's at about $65 billion, orders of magnitude above Moonshot's target. Even so, the projection is a reminder that open-weight models can be a real business rather than a loss-making ideological exercise.

How the revenue is being won is more contentious. Earlier this week Anthropic accused Moonshot of running a long-running distillation campaign that it says routed close to 300,000 requests from Kimi to Claude Opus, gathering more than 23 million responses for training. Moonshot has not responded publicly to the substance of the allegation.

articles.headline: Meta sued over Facebook and Instagram photos used to train its AI and build a face-recognition system
articles.subtitle: A proposed class action in Chicago alleges the company harvested biometric data without consent for NameTag, an unreleased feature for its smart glasses, and for the Emu and Muse Image models.
articles.body:
Parents and their children in Illinois and California have filed a proposed class action alleging that Meta illegally used their Facebook and Instagram photos to build NameTag, an unreleased face-recognition system for its smart glasses, and to train generative AI models including Emu and Muse Image.

The suit, filed last week in federal court in Chicago, claims Meta violated state privacy laws by extracting biometric information from people's photographs without notice or consent. WIRED reported in June that NameTag code had been embedded in the Meta glasses AI companion app, downloaded more than 50 million times. The system was designed to turn faces captured by the glasses into biometric signatures and match them against faceprints held in a database on the user's phone, configured to receive updates from Meta.

The complaint says those faceprints may be derived from Facebook and Instagram images, citing reporting that Meta employees claimed NameTag could identify people through their Meta connections or public Instagram accounts. It notes that Meta has not disclosed which images were used, saying that information rests only with the company. Meta said in June that it was "not building a central face database" but declined to answer whether NameTag would be opt-in or how long faceprints would be kept. Its chief technology officer, Andrew Bosworth, called WIRED's reporting "incredibly misleading" and later described the feature as a good idea.

The complaint also targets Meta's image generator Muse Image, which this summer allowed users to create images based on other people's public Instagram accounts. The company removed the feature within days.

articles.headline: US lawmakers move on AI safety as Trump says the risk of extinction doesn't worry him 'at all'
articles.subtitle: Bipartisan bills on rogue systems and superintelligence land in Congress while California signs youth chatbot rules. Asked in Dallas about warnings from researchers, the president said the priority is beating China.
articles.body:
Warnings from current and former researchers that AI could end in human extinction have begun producing legislation in Washington. On Wednesday, Democratic congressman Josh Gottheimer and Republican Mike Lawler introduced the Stop Rogue AI Act, a bipartisan House bill intended to stop AI systems operating without human oversight, giving federal agencies the means to detect dangerous systems on their networks and shut them down.

Independent senator Bernie Sanders and Democratic representative Greg Casar renewed their push for a bill that would ban the development and deployment of artificial superintelligence and pause AI development until federal safety rules are in place. Republican senator Ted Cruz told ABC's The View that "we've got to put some guardrails on it", and said he is working on legislation with Amy Klobuchar and Senate majority leader John Thune.

## The White House position

Asked in Dallas about the warnings, President Donald Trump was dismissive. "No, it doesn't worry me at all," he said, arguing the greater risk is losing the technology race: "I worry that if we don't win at AI, we'll find ourselves in a very difficult situation." He said the United States holds a lead of roughly a year over China. Bloomberg has reported that OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman has raised internally the possibility of slowing development of the most powerful models.

## California acts

Governor Gavin Newsom signed a package of measures imposing time limits and safety requirements on chatbots used by minors, including parental notifications when a child disables safety settings, mental health resources, independent child safety audits and annual risk assessments. The laws also bar social media platforms from giving under-16s "addictive features" such as autoplay and algorithmic feeds — a provision the Electronic Frontier Foundation called a functional ban on social media for teenagers.
